maya (sec-eng): Heads up — Snyk raised CVE-2025-2334 on our azure-keywrap dependency used in the KMS adapter. It flags key unwrap timing leak. Scanner attached output.

scanner-bot: SNYK-CRYPTO-XXXX: azure-keywrap <=1.3.2 contains timing side-channel in key unwrap APIs. More info: https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-CRYPTO-XXXX

oliver (platform): Is this actually used in production? Our KMS adapter does envelope encryption with customer KEKs in Azure Key Vault; azure-keywrap is only pulled by the local dev shim for testing.

maya (sec-eng): Correct — prod builds use azure-kv-client v4 which talks to Key Vault over REST and relies on Azure's server-side wrap/unwrap. The vulnerable lib appears in devtools/docker-image for local integration tests and in a small internal CLI used by some infra devs.

jen (sre): Can we confirm the vulnerable code path is never executed with customer keys? If it's only in dev containers we might be able to mitigate with a temporary denylist for CI and a risk acceptance for a short period.

maya (sec-eng): I've reproduced it locally. The local shim calls wrap/unwrap directly which invokes azure-keywrap. So there's a non-prod but still internal exposure. Impact: attacker with local container access could attempt timing attacks — low-likelihood, medium-impact for internal keys.

sam (product-sec): Proposed workaround: block the dev CLI image from running in prod clusters, rotate any internal test keys, and add stricter audit logging for Key Vault activity. We should consider a temporary allowlist in Snyk/Dependabot until we can bump the dev shim to a patched dependency.

oliver (platform): Sounds reasonable. Timeline: I can cut a patch bump to azure-keywrap 1.3.3 in devtools and rebuild the docker image today (ETA 4h). CI will still fail until we update the image tags in a few repos.

maya (sec-eng): For the formal risk acceptance: requesting temporary exception for CI false positive on prod scans for 72h while patch rollout completes. Compensating controls: remove image from prod, rotate test keys, disable CLI auto-login, and add Key Vault audit forwarding to SIEM for the next 30 days.

jen (sre): +1 for 72h window. I'll create a firewall rule to prevent the dev CLI image from being pulled by prod nodes and add a monitor for unusual unwrap requests.

sam (product-sec): Approving temporary acceptance with conditions above. Please add the exceptions ticket in Jira: SEC-5472 and include list of repos affected.

maya (sec-eng): Added SEC-5472 with details and mitigation checklist. I'll follow up once the images are rebuilt and tags updated.

oliver (platform): Pushed patched images: devtools:2025-04-12-azkw. PRs opened in infra/* to bump tags. Link: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/devtools/pull/128

maya (sec-eng): Verified in CI that the new image removes the vulnerable package. Closing the exception early. Thanks everyone :tada: 

sam (product-sec): Nice! Can we add an automated check to prevent vulnerable libs in dev images going forward?

maya (sec-eng): Filed follow-up SEC-5501 to add image scanning gating on release pipelines.

scanner-bot: Note: SNYK-CRYPTO-XXXX marked as ignored for SEC-5472 until 1789030000 per request by maya (sec-eng).
